items.title: Parents warned to keep kids off e-scooters in Mississauga
items.summary: Following news that 10 children died last year in Canada from e-scooter and e-bike injuries, Mississauga is reminding parents to keep kids off the micro-mobility devices. If used properly and in the right places, e-scooters can be a convenient way for residents and visitors aged 16 or older to move around the city, the City of Mississauga said in a press release today. “These devices can make it easier to connect to transit, travel to school or work, or complete everyday errands without a car,” the city said. ” The Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program said 10 kids died from e-bike or e-scooter injuries in 2025, six of them in Ontario. Twelve more patients were admitted to intensive care units and 26 were treated in the hospital for more than two days. The total number of severe e-scooter and e-bike injuries last year involving prolonged hospital stays, ICU admissions or death for paediatric patients was 57. E-scooter injuries among Mississauga residents are increasing, the city said. Emergency department visits involving children aged 15 and under on e-scooters more than doubled, from 34 visits in 2023 to 72 visits in 2024, the city said.

items.title: Mississauga's Leslie Log House Turns 200
items.summary: LESLIE LOG HOUSE BEFORE RELOCATION, 1980. How many people have driven by the historic log house on Mississauga Road? Have you stopped in for a visit? Surrounded by a remnant orchard (the former Riviere Fruit Farm), to some people the log house feels oddly placed – oriented at a slight angle to the road, with its “back” turned to the road (it’s front door faces away from Mississauga Road). Long-time residents may remember a time when the log house was not there. It was moved here in 1994. But this venerable old building, now owned by the City of Mississauga and home to the Streetsville Historical Society and Archives, is 200 years old this year! That is a milestone that relatively few buildings reach. An event was hosted on Saturday, August 8 to celebrate this milestone for this significant heritage landmark. But what is the log house’s back story? ) LESLIE FAMILY DESCENDANTS AT THE 2011 OPENING OF THE LESLIE LOG HOUSE. The Leslie Log House, as we call it today, was built in 1826 by John Leslie (Senior). and his wife, Esther (nee Beatty) Leslie. Esther (1782-1867), who was originally from County Tyrone, Ireland, met her first husband, William Leslie, when he was stationed in Ireland.

items.title: DavidsTea returns to Square One after closing 6 years ago in Mississauga
items.summary: Tea lovers rejoice — DavidsTea is back in Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga. The tea merchant officially announced the reopening in a press release today. “We are delighted to bring the full DavidsTea experience to consumers at Square One with our premium tea collections, wide assortment of accessories and expert recommendations from our Tea Guides,” said Sarah Segal, the company’s chief executive officer and chief brand officer. The shop, located on level two by entrance eight in Square One, celebrated their grand opening on Aug. 2. “A huge thank you to everyone who came by our opening event at Square One,” DavidsTea said on Instagram. ” Customers seemed thrilled with the shop’s return. “So happy to have you back close to home,” one person wrote on Instagram. “The store is beautiful and the staff is amazing! ” DavidsTea shut down 82 locations across Canada amid financial struggles in 2020, but last year the company announced a comeback. Stores were planned for Quebec City, Montreal and a location opened at the Oshawa Centre in June.

items.title: Mississauga Shelter Staff Say the $25 Adoption Push Isn't Skipping Any Steps
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, staff at Mississauga Animal Services say the screening process for adopting a pet hasn't changed during the shelter's ongoing $25 adoption event, even as the reduced fee draws more interest. The discount, running until Aug. 22 at the shelter's Central Parkway West location, cuts the standard adoption cost from roughly $280 plus tax for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus tax for cats and kittens down to a flat $25. Greg Madeley, the shelter's manager of animal care and wellbeing, told Mississauga.com the lower price is meant to free up kennel space, not shortcut the process of matching an animal with the right home. Mississauga.com reports staff still take steps before an animal leaves the shelter to make sure the pet and the prospective owner are a good fit. Among the animals up for adoption is Kaito, a senior dog who has been at the shelter since July 2023. Mississauga.com notes the shelter has taken in 18,986 animals since 2021.

items.title: Halton Police Say a Mississauga Man Filmed a Woman in an Oakville Fitting Room
items.summary: According to INsauga, Halton Regional Police have charged a Mississauga man after a woman reported being filmed inside a change room at the Winners store on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Oakville on July 22. Police say the woman confronted the man after noticing him, but he fled the store before officers arrived. INsauga reports investigators later identified and arrested the suspect, 34-year-old Jeffrey Abou-Mechrek of Mississauga, charging him with one count of voyeurism. He was released with a future court date in Milton. Police released a photo of Abou-Mechrek because investigators are concerned there may be additional victims they haven't yet identified. Anyone who believes they may have been victimized, or who has information about the case, is asked to contact Halton's 2 District Criminal Investigations Bureau.

items.title: DAVIDsTEA Picks Square One for Its Seventh Ontario Location as It Chases 25 Stores Nationwide
items.summary: According to a company announcement carried by Yahoo Finance, DAVIDsTEA has opened a new flagship store at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga, marking its seventh location in Ontario. The Montreal-based tea retailer says the store carries its full lineup of loose-leaf teas, signature collections and its in-store Tea Bar offering. The opening follows a new location in Oshawa Centre in June and strengthens the company's presence across the Greater Toronto Area. DAVIDsTEA says it plans to open two more stores this fall, which would bring its total store count to 25 across Canada by the end of the fiscal year. Company CEO Sarah Segal said the goal is to bring the full DAVIDsTEA experience to Square One shoppers through its tea collections, accessories and staff recommendations. Square One now joins other Ontario malls in the company's portfolio, including CF Toronto Eaton Centre, CF Sherway Gardens, Limeridge Mall, CF Rideau Centre, Masonville Place and Oshawa Centre.

items.title: Brampton landlord to face jail time after fire that killed pregnant woman, child in 2023
items.summary: An Ontario landlord has been sentenced to jail time after being convicted of seven charges following a Brampton fire that left a pregnant woman and her daughter dead more than three years ago.

items.title: Former Raptors coach fights Ontario over nearly $700K tax paid on multimillion-dollar home
items.summary: Former Toronto Raptors head coach Nick Nurse and his wife are embroiled in a legal dispute with the Ontario government over its refusal to reimburse the couple nearly $700,000 in foreign buyer tax they paid on their Mississauga home.
